The HTML file is not a document that opens an app: it is the app. The code, fonts and charts are all inside it, and nothing is downloaded when you use it.

Setting up: about ten minutes

  1. Extract the ZIP into a folder you will find again. A synced folder (iCloud Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive) is ideal.
  2. Double-click RentalPropertyTracker.html. It opens in Chrome, Edge, Safari or Firefox like a web page, and works offline from then on.
  3. Take the welcome tour. A few short slides on your properties, tenants, rent and backups.
  4. Follow the three steps on Home: add a property, add your tenants, then record rent and add your expenses.
  5. Download a backup from Settings & backup. Page 9 explains why it matters more than anything else here.

Want to look around first?

Choose Explore sample data on Home or in Settings & backup. A fictional landlord with three properties, a late tenant, a lease ending and a vacancy fills every screen, in a separate session. Return to my rentals brings back your own, untouched.

The idea

Every door, every month.

Home answers the monthly question: what came in, what went out, who still owes, and what needs you.

WordWhat it means
Cash flowRent and fees received − every expense, the mortgage included.
NOINet operating income: rent minus running costs, before the mortgage.
Cap rateA year of NOI ÷ what the property is worth.
Cash-on-cashA year of cash flow ÷ the cash you put in.

Properties & tenants

Add a property, then its tenants.

Properties → Add a property: its name, how many units, what it’s worth and the mortgage payment (roughly how much is interest). Then Tenants & leases → Add a tenant.

Tenant fieldWhat to enter
Rent and due dayThe monthly rent and the day it’s due. Rent appears on the rent roll every month.
Lease datesStart, and end (empty = month to month). Leases ending in 60 days show on Home.
Deposit, grace days, late feeLate after the grace days; your late fee is one click away when rent is late.

Each month

Record rent as it arrives.

The rent roll lists every unit: rent due, what arrived, and who’s late. Record a payment when it comes in; part payments are fine.

Expenses

Add an expense once: insurance, property taxes and HOA fees can repeat monthly or yearly on their own. Each one lands on its Schedule E line. Costs for all your rentals (bookkeeping software) go under General.

Your bank’s CSV

Import bank CSV: deposits that match a tenant become rent, withdrawals become expenses, mortgage payments and lines you imported before are skipped. You check every line first.

Money & taxes

What each property really earns.

Finances shows income, running costs, NOI and cash flow for every property side by side, for any dates. Profit & loss is the full statement; Schedule E is the tax worksheet.

Profit & lossPick the dates and a property, or all with a column each. Print or Export CSV for your accountant.
Schedule ERents and every expense line by property, for the year. Depreciation isn’t worked out: ask your tax pro.
Loan principalCounts in cash flow, not as an expense; it pays down the loan.

Tenants & paperwork

Charges, repairs and letters.

The landlord jobs that usually live on sticky notes, kept with your numbers.

Charge a tenant

Damage, utilities, cleaning, keys: list each item, set a pay-by date, then Bill prints a statement of charges. Record payment when it’s paid.

Repairs & letters

Log a repair or a tenant’s request; marked done with a cost, it goes into expenses. Letters & notices fills in 11 letters from your records; edit, print or copy.

The letters are starting points, not legal advice: notice periods and rules differ by state and city.

Keeping your rentals safe.

Everything lives in your browser, on your device. Nothing is sent anywhere, there is no account, and nobody else holds a copy, including us.

Your entries live in browser storage: please read

  • Everything you enter or import is saved automatically in that browser's local storage.
  • Clearing your cache, history or site data will permanently delete it.
  • It does not carry across browsers: data added in Chrome will not appear in Safari.
  • The HTML file does not contain your entries. Copying the file does not copy your data.

Do one of these. Ideally both.

Download backup: every browser

Settings & backup → Download backup. One JSON file holding every property, tenant, payment, expense, repair, charge and letter wording. Restore backup brings it back on any computer. The app reminds you when a backup is due.

Daily folder backup: Chrome or Edge

Choose a synced folder once (iCloud Drive, Dropbox, OneDrive, Google Drive) and a dated copy is written each day you make changes. Safari and Firefox do not offer this; use Download backup instead.

Moving to another computer

Copy the HTML file and your latest backup across, open the file, then Settings & backup → Restore backup.

When you need help

A few useful fixes.

What you seeWhat to do
It opens as code, not an appExtract the ZIP first, then right-click the file → Open with → your browser.
My numbers are goneCheck it is the same browser and profile you used before. Otherwise, Restore backup.
A tenant shows as late but paidCheck the payment’s For the month of: it may be recorded against another month.
Cash flow looks very negativeA yearly bill (property taxes, insurance) landed this month. Look at Finances for the year to date.
Deposits came in as skippedAdd your tenants first, then import again: deposits are matched to tenants by name or exact rent.
A tenant moved outEdit the lease and set the move-out date. Rent stops; their history stays.
Folder backup unavailableUse Chrome or Edge on a computer, or Download backup instead.
The currency is wrongSettings & backup → Currency, or type your own symbol. Amounts are not converted.
I want the tour againSettings & backup → Welcome tour → Show tour.
